newsitem.title: JAPAN: Kaneichi, units declared bankrupt by Osaka court.
newsitem.headline: Kaneichi, units declared bankrupt by Osaka court.

text.p: Japanese property firm Kaneichi and its four affiliates have been declared bankrupt by the Osaka District Court, a court official said on Tuesday.
Debts of the five firms totalled 204.58 billion yen, credit research firm Teikoku Databank Ltd said.
In late November, the Osaka-based realtor filed for special liquidation at the court. The company was a major borrower of funds from "jusen" housing loan companies which have now failed.
Company officials were not available for comment.

Kaneichi's borrowing escalated in the late 1980s when Japan's "economic bubble" of inflated land and stock prices was at its height, but with the end of the boom, it became unable to pay back its debts, Teikoku Databank said in a report.
